title: How do idempotent producers help achieve exactly-once semantics, and why does it matter?
shortTitle: How idempotent producers help achieve exactly-once semantics, and why it matters
keyPoints: Duplicates happen when the broker writes a record but the acknowledgement is lost, causing the producer to retry.
The idempotent producer assigns a producer id and per-partition sequence number so the broker drops duplicate retries.
Idempotence requires acks=all, retries > 0, and max.in.flight.requests.per.connection <= 5.
Idempotence alone gives exactly-once on one partition within one producer session.
Full exactly-once stacks transactions and read_committed consumers on top of idempotence.
Idempotence does not protect against application-level resends or external side effects.
In banking, a duplicated transfer is money created or destroyed -- removing retry duplicates is a correctness requirement.

s1_definition.oneliner: Idempotent producers remove retry duplicates on the write path, which is the essential first building block of end-to-end exactly-once.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Idempotent producer** -- the foundation of exactly-once on the write side; guarantees that a record sent once is written exactly once even if the producer retries after a lost acknowledgement.
- **Producer id** -- a unique identifier assigned by the broker to the producer session; used with the sequence number for deduplication.
- **Sequence number** -- a monotonically increasing per-partition counter the producer attaches to each record; if the broker sees a duplicate sequence, it acknowledges without writing.
- **Exactly-once semantics** -- each record is produced once, grouped writes are atomic, and consumers never see duplicates or partial results.
- **Transaction layer** -- builds on idempotence to add atomicity across partitions and tie offset commits to output records.
- **read_committed** -- consumer isolation level that only delivers committed transaction records, completing the exactly-once chain.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine Rajesh instructs National Bank of India to transfer fifty thousand rupees. The phone line drops before he hears done, so his app resends. An idempotent producer is like stamping each instruction with a unique serial number: the bank sees the same serial twice and files it only once, so Rajesh is debited exactly once, not twice. That single guarantee is the first brick of exactly-once; stacking transactions and read-committed on top makes the whole money movement happen once and only once.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Without Idempotence:
  Producer ──send──▶ Broker writes (offset 100)
           ◀──ACK LOST──
  Producer ──retry─▶ Broker writes AGAIN (offset 101)
                     DUPLICATE!

  With Idempotence:
  Producer ──send──▶ Broker writes (offset 100, PID=7, seq=5)
  (PID=7)  ◀──ACK LOST──
  Producer ──retry─▶ Broker checks: PID=7, seq=5 already written
  (seq=5)            ACK but NO WRITE
                     No duplicate!

  Exactly-Once Stack:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Layer 3: read_committed consumer        │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Layer 2: Transactional producer         │
  │          (atomic multi-partition write)  │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Layer 1: Idempotent producer (BASE)     │
  │          (PID + sequence dedup)         │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Idempotent producers are the foundation of exactly-once semantics because they eliminate the one unavoidable source of duplicates on the write path: retries after a lost acknowledgement. The broker gives the producer a unique producer id, and every record carries a per-partition sequence number. A retried record with a sequence the broker has already seen is acknowledged but never written again.

By itself, idempotence gives exactly-once on a single partition within one producer session. Full end-to-end exactly-once stacks transactions on top for atomic multi-partition writes, ties offset commits to output inside the same transaction, and uses read_committed consumers. The idempotent producer is the base brick; transactions and read-committed complete the structure.

At National Bank of India, every producer runs idempotent so Priya is never double-charged. For the settle-and-charge flow, Rajesh uses a transactional producer that writes the settlement event and the fee event and commits the trade offset in one transaction. The billing consumer reads with read_committed.

Remember one sentence: idempotent producers make the word exactly-once honest on the write side by using a producer id and sequence number to drop retry duplicates, and they are the non-negotiable first layer on which transactions build the complete guarantee.
